standard_prerequisites.name: The adjunction of the two functors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the construction of the functors F and G and their adjunction established earlier
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the pair of functors whose derived functors are compared and the identity of the composite on the module side.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fully faithful adjunctions
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that an adjunction whose unit or counit is an isomorphism is fully faithful, which is how full faithfulness of the derived functor is concluded.

standard_prerequisites.name: K-injective representatives
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the derived functor can be computed on a K-injective representative, which is what makes the composite computation available.

core_obligations: Reduction to representatives (proof lines 2939-2948): the author recalls that the right derived functor is computed by applying the functor to a K-injective representative, and sets up the comparison of the composite of the two derived functors with the identity.

The composite computation (proof lines 2949-2951): evaluating on a suitable representative complex, the composite of the two functors is the identity because the two functors are inverse on the module side by the adjunction established earlier.
Full faithfulness (proof lines 2952-2953): the cited criterion for adjunctions then gives full faithfulness of the derived functor, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Compute the composite of the two derived functors on such a representative.
Apply the criterion for full faithfulness of an adjunction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the derived functor arising from the Gabriel-Popescu adjunction is fully faithful (statement lines 2921-2937). The proof is a complete argument: the derived functor is computed on K-injective representatives (proof lines 2939-2948); on such a representative the composite of the two functors is the identity because the functors are inverse to each other on the module side (proof lines 2949-2951); and the criterion for full faithfulness of an adjunction then gives the conclusion (proof lines 2952-2953). The non-formal content is the computation of the composite on representatives. The claim is H2.
